_note: Per-patient incremental acquisition cost vector for B1. Every number is either quoted from a source or derived from quoted numbers by the formula given. Retrieved 2026-10-09. Clinicopathologic data (incl. pathologic stage) and the H&E glass slide itself are standard of care after resection and carry zero incremental cost.

slides_per_patient.derivation: 4,532 WSI feature files / 1,310 patients with WSI in the analysis cohort (experiments/lung_missingness/prepared/summary.json)

scanner_ownership.quote: cost per scan was calculated to be between $0.55 and $19.53

scan_staff.quote: staffing ... contributes $0.79-0.92 to the cost per slide scanned

storage.derivation: 2 GB per single-z-plane WSI x $1M per PB on-premise storage including redundancy

low.derivation: WTS consumables EUR 278 per case (consumables only; excludes personnel, equipment, data) converted at an assumed 1.08 USD/EUR; a lower bound

high.derivation: WES/WTS test cost input (US list price, includes the exome component); an upper bound

context.quote: Microcosting estimates from four studies range between $9,309 USD and $1,914 USD (WGTS)

wsi.value: about 1 min scanning per slide; same working day
wsi.quote: mean scan time of 1 min per slide (modelling assumption)

rna.quote: turnaround time for WGTS ... < 10-14 working days

wsi_per_slide.derivation: 2,116-2,923 t CO2eq for 1 year of storage of 28,932,624 slides (France, nuclear-dominated grid); storage-dominated, per slide-year

rna_per_patient_compute_only.derivation: 0.001-0.1 kgCO2e per million reads for alignment x 50 M reads; wet-lab reagents, instruments and shipping NOT included

rna_wetlab.note: No peer-reviewed per-sample life-cycle assessment of clinical RNA-seq identified; reported as a gap

central.derivation: midpoints of the WSI and RNA ranges; kappa = 36.1
